assumptions: TraceTuner's indel detection on its calibration table.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does this trace split into two reads of different length, as a heterozygous indel does?

description: Ask whether a Sanger trace splits into TWO READS OF DIFFERENT LENGTH, which is what a heterozygous insertion or deletion does: clean up to the indel, then a superposition of two sequences offset by its length. This is not mixed-base calling — that asks whether two BASES sit at one position and is blind to a length difference. Emits where the split starts, how long it is, and the two allele sequences the trace deconvolves into, so a pipeline can gate on the answer or carry either allele onward.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

breakpoint_scan.description: skip the search and measure the indel at this scan position on the x axis. -1 searches for it.

document.description: which trace file to read: its name (`read_F.ab1`) or its project file id. LEAVE IT EMPTY to run on the chromatogram tab that is open, in which case the answer also appears in the rail. A file id is project-specific, so a template ships this unset.

quality_value_reading.description: corrected = read the quality values as TraceTuner's own header declares them, which is the only reading that can detect anything; upstream = reproduce the program as shipped, whose detector never fires.

table.description: the instrument and polymer the quality scale was calibrated on. There is no universal default: a base scores differently under a different table, and the detector gates on a quality JUMP.

name: detect_trace_indel

found.description: whether a heterozygous indel was detected. Wire it into a gate

longAllele.description: the allele with the extra bases, from the breakpoint on. N marks a position the deconvolution would not commit to, not a low-quality base

qualityJump.description: the drop in quality values across the breakpoint. It must exceed 7 for a position to be considered at all, so this is what a negative answer is checkable against

report.description: the whole finding, including the size in scans and the stutter verdict

shortAllele.description: the allele without them, from the breakpoint on

sizeInBases.description: how many bases the longer allele carries that the shorter one does not

startsAtBase.description: the 1-based base the split starts at, or 0 when none was found
